## Goal

Extend the pure shared helpers so that a theme carries typographic mood and text
placement as well as colours. Both files stay free of DOM and Node APIs, because
the browser loads them unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/shared/palette.ts`: add `export function rgbToHsl(c: Rgb): [number, number, number]` returning hue 0-360, saturation 0-1 and lightness 0-1.
- `src/shared/theme.ts`:
  - `export type Mood = "serif" | "grotesque" | "mono"` and `export type Placement = "top-left" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-right"`.
  - `export function pickMood(palette: Rgb[]): Mood`: empty palette gives `"serif"`; mean saturation below 0.15 gives `"mono"`; hue of `palette[0]` below 70 or at least 330 gives `"serif"`; anything else gives `"grotesque"`.
  - `export function calmestRegion(lums: number[], cols: number, rows: number): Placement`: splits the row-major luminance grid into four quadrants and returns the one with the lowest variance. Ties resolve in the order bottom-left, bottom-right, top-left, top-right. A grid whose length is not `cols * rows` returns `"bottom-left"`.
  - `export function fontStack(mood: Mood): string` returns a system font stack per mood, with no web font URLs.
  - `Theme` gains `mood: Mood` and `placement: Placement`. `neutralTheme()` returns `mood: "serif"` and `placement: "bottom-left"`.
  - `deriveTheme(palette, lums?, cols?, rows?)` fills `mood` from `pickMood` and `placement` from `calmestRegion` when a grid is supplied, otherwise `"bottom-left"`. A call with one argument still works.
  - `themeToCss` appends `;--font:<fontStack(mood)>` after the five colour properties.

## Out of scope

- Canvas sampling and applying the theme to the document (W1-04).
- Any change to `src/server.ts`.

## Done

- The exports listed above exist with those signatures. `luminance`, `contrastRatio`, `toHex` and `extractPalette` keep their current behaviour.
- `node --test tests/theme.test.ts` passes with the four tests listed in the header.
- `tests/slice.test.ts` still passes unchanged: `deriveTheme([])` deep-equals `neutralTheme()` and the `--ink:#f2efe9;--paper:#101114` prefix is preserved.
- Neither shared file imports from `node:` or references `document` or `window`.
